Core_Definition: The commercial insurance business model where premiums are eagerly collected for decades, but when a catastrophic disaster strikes, armies of adjusters and fine-print exclusions are deployed to deny 90% of claims.
Core_Mechanism: Asymmetric contract complexity and attrition; insurance carriers use unreadable, 80-page policy exclusions ('acts of God', 'sub-surface water seepage', 'anti-concurrent causation clauses') to legally evade payment.
Typical_Contexts: Florida homeowners losing houses to hurricanes and having claims denied because the wind blew before the water rose; health insurers retroactively rescinding coverage for 'undisclosed pre-existing acne'
